module.name: BCM2_02_Collective Benefit
module.description: Extended axiomatics of collective benefit including destruction logic (A43–A46), comprising dispositional and behavior-based components.

A1.title: Chapter Designation and Context
A1.text: The module BCM2_02_Collective Benefit formalizes the logic of benefit and disbenefit arising from collective goods. Collective benefit exists when goods or states are non-excludable and non-rivalrous. It arises independently of individual participation and operates across all FEPSDE dimensions (financial, psychological, physical, social, ecological, digital).

A2.title: Scope of Applicability
A2.text: The module applies to collectives of any size: teams, organizations, societies, or digital communities. Collective benefit includes both benefit gains and disbenefits and exerts effects even on actors who do not contribute themselves. Representation takes place across all FEPSDE dimensions.

A3.title: Objective and Function within the Model
A3.text: The objective is the formal representation of collective benefit as a benefit and disbenefit function. The module defines the axioms governing collective action: non-excludability, non-rivalry, free-riding, punishment, reward, and norm stability. It forms the foundation for governance architectures and intervention designs.

axioms.title: FEPSDE Structure
axioms.formula: N_{kol}(t) = \\sum_{d \\in \\{fin, psy, phy, soc, eco, dig\\}} G_d^{kol}(t)
axioms.description: Collective benefit covers all FEPSDE dimensions: financial, psychological, physical, social, ecological, and digital.

axioms.title: Context Weights
axioms.description: The dimensions of collective benefit are weighted differently depending on context.

axioms.title: Pain/Gain Separation
axioms.description: Benefit gains (gain) and losses (pain) are modeled strictly separately.

axioms.title: Pain–Gain Asymmetry
axioms.description: Losses have a stronger impact than gains of equal magnitude.

axioms.title: Pain–Gain Complementarity
axioms.description: Pain and gain must not be mixed or netted against each other.

axioms.title: Temporal Conditionality
axioms.description: Collective benefit unfolds across four time horizons: instantaneous, short-term, medium-term, and long-term.

axioms.title: Uncertainty Modulation
axioms.description: Uncertainty changes the time preferences of collective benefit. Environmental, epistemic, interpersonal, and institutional uncertainties act directly.

axioms.title: Belief-Based Cooperation
axioms.description: Cooperation within the collective emerges from beliefs about the contribution behavior of other actors.

axioms.title: Actor Types in the Collective
axioms.description: Different actor types exist: pure egoists, conditional cooperators, and pure cooperators.

axioms.title: Life Changing Events
axioms.description: Societal shocks or life changing events shift collective benefit irreversibly.

axioms.title: Non-Excludability
axioms.description: No one can be fully excluded from collective benefit.

axioms.title: Non-Rivalry
axioms.description: Use by one person does not reduce the benefit of others.

axioms.title: Commons Rivalry
axioms.description: With scarce collective resources, rivalry arises (tragedy of the commons).

axioms.title: Social Benefit and Disbenefit
axioms.description: Social norms generate both social benefit and social disbenefit.

axioms.title: Financial Benefit and Disbenefit
axioms.description: Financial resources create security, but also costs such as taxes.

axioms.title: Psychological Benefit and Disbenefit
axioms.description: Collectives create psychological safety, but also stress through pressure and expectation.

axioms.title: Physical Benefit and Disbenefit
axioms.description: Physical safety can be created collectively, but restrictions as well.

axioms.title: Digital Benefit and Disbenefit
axioms.description: Digital infrastructure provides access, but also generates surveillance and control costs.

axioms.title: Ecological Benefit and Disbenefit
axioms.description: Collective environmental protection yields benefits; ecological constraints can create disbenefits.

axioms.title: Cumulative Experience
axioms.description: Societal experience shapes collective benefit over time; gains and losses act asymmetrically.

axioms.title: Intergenerational Effect
axioms.description: Collective benefit operates across generations and is intergenerationally relevant.

axioms.title: Identity Complementarity
axioms.description: Identification with a collective amplifies collective benefit.

axioms.title: Institutional Embeddedness
axioms.description: Institutions shape benefit and disbenefit.

axioms.title: Resilience
axioms.description: Collective benefit remains stable even under disruptions.

axioms.title: Emergence and Tipping Points
axioms.description: Collective benefit can abruptly collapse or rise due to tipping points.

axioms.title: Fairness and Distribution
axioms.description: Unequal distributions reduce collective benefit.

axioms.title: Ethics and Privacy
axioms.description: Collective benefit must comply with ethical standards and privacy.

axioms.title: Transparency
axioms.description: Collective benefit must be transparently documented and verifiable.

axioms.title: Bias Control
axioms.description: Bias in the measurement of collective benefit must be limited.

axioms.title: Misuse Prevention
axioms.description: Collective benefit must be protected against misuse and archived.

axioms.title: Decentralized Punishment
axioms.formula: U_p = U_p - \sum_d c_d(s), \\; U_d = U_d - m \cdot c_p(s)
axioms.description: Decentralized punishment occurs only when social norms exist, punishment is proportionate, and marginal benefits are greater than or equal to marginal costs.

axioms.title: Centralized Punishment
axioms.description: Centralized punishment is effective only when institutions possess accurate information and sanctions are perceived as legitimate.

axioms.title: Whistleblowing
axioms.description: Whistleblowing occurs only when expected benefits exceed expected costs and sufficient protection is ensured.

axioms.title: Preventive Conformity
axioms.description: Strong norms combined with proportionate sanctions lead to preventive conformity without the need for actual punishment.

axioms.title: Institutional Quality
axioms.description: The effectiveness of centralized punishment depends on institutional quality, fairness, and informational accuracy.

axioms.title: Elite Role Modeling
axioms.description: Role-model behavior by elites strengthens or weakens norm conformity and the legitimacy of sanctions.

axioms.title: Positive Incentives
axioms.description: Rewards for conforming behavior stabilize collective benefit.

axioms.title: Rehabilitation
axioms.description: After punishment, reintegration into the collective is necessary to restore normative equilibrium.

axioms.title: Inequality Effects
axioms.description: Punishments affect actors differently depending on status and available resources.

axioms.title: Mis-Punishment
axioms.description: Erroneous punishment destroys trust and institutional legitimacy.

axioms.title: Cultural Variation
axioms.description: The form and acceptance of punishment depend on cultural norms.

axioms.title: Dynamic Adaptation
axioms.description: Punishment dynamically adapts to defection rates and contextual conditions.

A5.title: Requirements
A5.text: Modeling collective benefit requires data on individual contributions and collective outcomes. In addition, indicators for norm strength, cultural acceptance, institutional quality, fairness, inequality, and statistical error rates are necessary.

A6.title: Integration
A6.text: The module 7235 integrates as follows: 7232 (Meta) and 9232 (Standard); 7234 (Individual Benefit) and 7236 (Identity Benefit); 7240 (Awareness) and 7243 (Willingness); 8904 (Context Logic) and 7257 (Segment Logic); 7457 (Life Journeys) and 7256 (Behavioral Change Journey); uncertainty modules 9485–9495 and 9492 (Complexity); 9250 (Intervention Toolkit) and 9251 (Watchdog); 9477 (Statistical Modeling), 9479 (Player Types), and 9480 (Game Theory).

A7.title: Module Limitations
A7.text: The module does not model individual benefit preferences; this is covered in module 7234. Full simulations require context and uncertainty modules. Without incorporating institutional quality (A35), no reliable statements can be made about centralized punishment.

A8.title: Versioning
A8.text: Version 1.0: Introduction of FEPSDE structure. Version 2.0: Integration of pain/gain, time, uncertainty. Version 2.5: Expansion with governance and transparency. Version 3.0: Added punishment, incentive, and stability axioms (A31–A42). Version 3.1: Extension with A43–A46 (destruction logic including Dark Triad and behavioral indicators).

A9.title: Citation
A9.text: Fehr and Gächter (2000ff.): public goods experiments, cooperation and punishment. Ostrom (1990): governing the commons and collective goods. FehrAdvice & Partners AG: Behavioral Change Model BCM 2.0/2.1.

A10.title: License
A10.text: Use according to FehrAdvice BCM 2.0 licensing. Citation required for reuse.

axioms_extension.title: Antisocial Punishment (Destruction Condition)
axioms_extension.description: Punishment without legitimacy and without normative coherence destroys collective benefit.

axioms_extension.title: Dispositional Amplification (Dark Triad Extension I)
axioms_extension.description: Machiavellianism (M), narcissism (N), and psychopathy (P) amplify the intensity of antisocial punishment. Each component affects legitimacy, norm coherence, and punishment differently.

axioms_extension.title: Behavior-Based Indicators (A43 Decalogue Extension II)
axioms_extension.description: Ten micro-social behavioral patterns signal the activation of antisocial punishment.

axioms_extension.title: Destruction Function with Disposition and Behavior (A43-DTX Extension III)
axioms_extension.formula: Pun_anti_DTX = Pun * (1 - Legit) * (1 - NormCoh) * (1 + Θ_DT) * (1 + Θ_Beh)
axioms_extension.description: Extended destruction condition: antisocial punishment is multiplicatively amplified by dispositional (Dark Triad) and behavior-based (A43 Decalogue) factors.
axioms_extension.empirical_reference: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM 2.1 Simulation Engine

integration_v31.title: Integration
integration_v31.description: Describes the functional embedding of module 7235 – Collective Benefit – in the overall architecture of the Behavioral Change Model 2.0. It considers all dependencies to meta, utility, context, uncertainty, and intervention modules, as well as the new destruction axioms A43–A46.

sections.heading: 1. Meta and Structure Modules

modules.name: BCM2_00_META
modules.role: Fundamental axioms and logical framework conditions of the model.

modules.name: BCM2_00_STD
modules.role: Standardization of variable and function notations.

sections.integration_logic: Meta and standard modules provide the formal frame for all benefit functions; axioms A1–A7 of 7235 directly reference the base concepts defined there.

sections.heading: 2. Utility Modules

modules.name: Individual Benefit
modules.link: Aggregation of individual contributions into N_kol.

sections.integration_logic: 7235 represents the collective aggregation layer that links 7234 (individual) and 7236 (identity).

sections.heading: 3. Awareness and Willingness Modules

modules.name: Awareness
modules.role: Perception of collective benefit; influences Legit(t).

modules.name: Willingness
modules.role: Readiness to act to maintain N_kol; responds to Pun_anti.

sections.integration_logic: Perception and willingness functions act as feedback loops: if awareness or willingness decreases, Pun_anti increases and ΔN_kol becomes negative.

sections.heading: 4. Context and Segment Modules

modules.name: Context Logic
modules.role: Defines situational conditions for legitimacy and norm coherence.

modules.name: Segment Logic
modules.role: Computes Θ_DT and Θ_Beh depending on context and segment.

modules.name: Life Journeys
modules.role: Temporal variation of collective benefit perception.

modules.name: Behavioral Change Journey
modules.role: Phase model for change processes of collective structures.

sections.integration_logic: Context and segmentation determine weights ω_d(t) and the dynamics of Legit(t) and NormCoh(t) over time and life phase.

sections.heading: 5. Uncertainty and Complexity Modules

modules.name: Uncertainty Modules
modules.role: Modulate β_τ and influence long-run stability of collective benefit.

modules.name: Complexity
modules.role: Analyzes system robustness against Pun_anti disturbances.

sections.integration_logic: Uncertainty reduces time preference and amplifies the impact of A43; complexity modulates system resilience (A24).

sections.heading: 6. Governance and Intervention Modules

modules.name: Intervention Toolkit
modules.role: Provides action options for A36–A38 (role modeling, incentives, rehabilitation).

modules.name: Watchdog
modules.role: Monitors Pun_anti_DTX, Θ_DT, and Θ_Beh as an early-warning system.

sections.integration_logic: A43–A46 provide inputs for Watchdog 9251. If a threshold is exceeded, 9250 activates suitable intervention pathways.

sections.heading: 7. Empirical and Game-Theoretic Validation

modules.name: Statistical Modeling
modules.role: Validates empirical values of Pun_anti_DTX and ΔN_kol.

modules.name: Player Types
modules.role: Determines segment types (cooperative, egoistic, conditional) for ρ_K.

modules.name: Game Theory
modules.role: Computes strategic equilibria under punishment conditions.

sections.integration_logic: Data from 7235 (N_kol, Pun_anti_DTX) serve as inputs for experimental and game-theoretic simulations.

sections.heading: 8. Extension A43–A46 (Destruction Logic)
sections.description: The destruction axioms A43–A46 connect structural, dispositional, and behavioral layers.

linkage.A43: Defines the base condition for antisocial punishment.
linkage.A46: Links all factors into the destruction function Pun_anti_DTX.

sections.integration_logic: These axioms are directly coupled with Watchdog 9251 and Segment Logic 7257 to detect destructive dynamics early and compensate via Intervention Toolkit 9250.

sections.heading: 9. Integration Outcome
sections.summary: 7235 is the central aggregation module for collective benefit, disbenefit, and destruction functions. It links individual, collective, and identity-level utility layers with context, uncertainty, and intervention logics. Through A43–A46, it serves as the interface for detecting, quantifying, and stabilizing collective dynamics.
